root_cause.text: The USB core unanchors the URB before invoking the completion callback, so after the first completion the URB is no longer anchored in `parent->rx_submitted`, causing `gs_can_close()` to miss freeing it when calling `usb_kill_anchored_urbs()`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "the USB framework unanchors the URB before the complete function is called. This means that once an in-URB has been completed, it is no longer anchored and is ultimately not released in gs_can_close()." The patch adds `usb_anchor_urb(urb, &parent->rx_submitted);` in the callback before resubmission to re-anchor it.

intent_record.how: The URB is now anchored to the rx_submitted list before submission, enabling proper tracking and cleanup of pending URBs, which prevents resource leaks and potential use-after-free scenarios upon device disconnection.

candidates.rationale: The URB is submitted without being anchored to parent->rx_submitted, so after its completion callback the USB core unanchors it (if it were anchored), but since it was never anchored, it remains invisible to usb_kill_anchored_urbs() in gs_can_close(), causing a use-after-free or resource leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: The URB is submitted via usb_submit_urb without first being anchored to parent->rx_submitted. The USB core unanchors the URB after the completion callback, so the URB is not tracked in the anchored list. Consequently, gs_can_close() misses freeing it when calling usb_kill_anchored_urbs(), leading to a use-after-free or resource leak.
